sentences.text: Arandaspis was a small creature, estimated to have reached a length of 12 to 14 centimeters, though some comparisons suggest it measured approximately 15 centimeters.
Its body was covered in rows of knobbly armored scutes, which served as protective scales.
Comparisons with other early ostracoderms suggest that Arandaspis lacked paired fins and relied on a horizontally flattened tail for propulsion.
Arandaspis represents one of the earliest records of an Ordovician vertebrate from the southern hemisphere and is considered one of the oldest known vertebrates.
The name Arandaspis honors the local Indigenous Australian people known as the Aranda, now called the Arrernte.
The genus Arandaspis was described by Ritchie and Gilbert-Tomlinson in 1977, following the discovery of fossils in the Stairway Sandstone near Alice Springs, Australia, in 1959.
Although it lacked jaws, Arandaspis may have had movable mouth plates used like lips to suck up food particles, and the low position of the mouth suggests that it fed on the sea floor.
Arandaspis lived during the Early Ordovician, approximately 480 to 470 million years ago, specifically from the Floian to the Darriwilian stages between 477.1 and 458.2 million years ago.
